output.title: Anonymise first, automate second
output.body:
Before you automate a portfolio workflow, decide one thing first: will any document that enters the process still contain customer identifiers? If the answer is yes, stop there and anonymise or mask a sample before you test AI against it. That includes quotes, invoices, contracts, case notes, and the nicer-looking summary slides. The point is not to make compliance disappear; it is to reduce exposure before anything automated touches the file.

For a small business owner, the practical check is simple. Pick one recurring workflow you already handle in email, CRM, a shared drive, or a Zapier/Make step. Then ask: where does the document first leave your control, and who reviews it before anything automated happens? If human review is already part of the path, keep it. If the workflow depends on identifiable data, anonymise a sample first and use that as the test set.

This is a governance choice, not an AI feature and not legal advice. Once the sample is clean, you have a better input for deciding whether automation fits at all. That is usually where the tidy answer starts.
